summary: 60-foot Aermotor fire tower in Bath County, Virginia, built late 1930s; listed standing; NHLR-registered 2017; administrator and public access unclear.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor tower with a wrap-around catwalk; second of two towers in Bath County

evidence.supports: built in the late 1930s; 60-foot Aermotor tower; second of two towers in Bath County
evidence.quote: Built in the late 1930s, this 60' Aermotor tower is the second of two towers in Bath County.

listed as a standing tower, NHLR US 1165, VA 31

evidence.supports: located in the George Washington National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR's table gives 3,844 ft (1,172 m) and its description says 3819 feet. The story reports both figures and does not choose between them.

NHLR names American Tower Corporation as administrator; the eastern lookouts page places the tower in the George Washington National Forest. Both are cited; no source explains how they fit together, so the fact keeps NHLR's wording with a 'per NHLR' tag.
NHLR says 'late 1930s' in its description and '1930s' in its table. No exact year is given in any source, so no built event is recorded.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: only three sources read and the eastern lookouts page for this tower is a heading only (name, county, forest). No staffing history, no fires, no visit or access information was found. Not to be confused with other Duncan Knob sites in the George Washington National Forest near Mount Jackson and Massanutten (about 38.7 N, -78.6 W), which are different places; this record is the Bath County site at 38.164, -79.705. A community Facebook post about a former attendant was not used because only a truncated snippet was readable. The access field is omitted because no source says whether the public may climb the tower.
